login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry unless explicitly revoked.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected throughout Logto token usage docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same valid access token as replay by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without an `nbf` claim, or lack of explicit `nbf` enforcement, is spec-compliant because `nbf` is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing `nbf` enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: This is by design and changes which verification endpoint should be used.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured, Logto uses it as the audience when the `resource` parameter is omitted.
oidc_jwt.source: Role-based access control and global API resource docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful issuance without explicit `resource` as overbroad authorization when a default API resource exists.

oidc_jwt.description: MFA validation is bypassed for users signing in via enterprise SSO because the upstream IdP is treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing Logto-side MFA challenge after enterprise SSO as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag an old token retaining old scopes before expiry as stale-cache vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions that were not part of the original authorization request do not appear through refresh alone; a new OAuth authorization flow is required.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing newly granted scopes on refresh as a bug if they were outside the original request set.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not fetched directly from the authorization code flow; user flows require refresh token flow to obtain organization tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: A missing organization token immediately after code exchange is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs retain their original scopes until they expire, even after permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions immediately.

oidc_jwt.description: After an admin rotates signing keys, tokens signed by the new current key are expected to validate.
oidc_jwt.note: Admin-authorized trust-anchor changes are by design; only old-key acceptance after intended cutover and cache expiry is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: After signing key rotation, previously issued tokens signed by the previous key may remain valid while the previous key is still retained.
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag old-key acceptance after the previous key should no longer be trusted or after explicit removal/expiry expectations.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin-initiated signing key rotation is by design and authorizes the new trust anchor.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful validation under the newly rotated key as trust-anchor substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing Logto user when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges on matching email are documented behavior, not accidental cross-user collision.

oidc_jwt.description: Social connectors sharing the same target represent the same identity provider and can lead to the same Logto account outcome.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-connector identity merging for the same target is expected; different targets split identity pools.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` are not revoked by default and may continue until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Refresh-token usability after logout can be by design when offline access was granted.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Use introspection or userinfo semantics for opaque tokens; do not apply JWT-only oracles.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST set the token request `resource` parameter to the exact registered API identifier URI. Logto requires exact resource-indicator matching per RFC 8707; missing, shortened, or wildcard-like values do not match and will change token type or audience semantics.

For oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST request a `resource` (and `organization_id` when testing organization-scoped APIs) so Logto issues a JWT access token. If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT, which is a different protocol path and will invalidate JWT-based test assumptions.

For I5 scope tests, requested `scope` values MUST exactly match permission names defined in Logto. Scope names are exact string matches only; prefixes, abbreviations, and wildcard-like values are not supported.

For I5 organization-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST include `organization_id` in token requests when testing organization permissions or organization-level API resources. Without `organization_id`, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced.

For I5 mixed-scope tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT combine global API permissions with organization permissions in the same authorization expectation. Logto documents these as distinct models; organization permissions and organization-level API permissions are defined by the organization template and cannot be mixed with global API permissions.

For I5 permission-change sequences, the fuzzer MUST account for Logto's scope subset rule: a newly issued token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test enlarged permissions, request the superset of candidate scopes in the original authorization request; otherwise missing scopes after refresh are by design, not an authorization-binding failure.

For I3 role/policy tightening tests, the fuzzer MUST use a NEW token issuance after the config change. Existing JWTs keep their old scopes until expiry; only newly issued tokens reflect reduced permissions immediately.

For I3 default-audience tests, if the tenant has a default API resource configured, omitting `resource` causes Logto to use that default audience. The fuzzer MUST explicitly control whether `resource` is omitted or set, otherwise audience results may reflect default-resource behavior rather than a validation bug.

For I2 expired-token and future-token tests, the fuzzer MUST include a control request using a valid token obtained through the same flow. A failed attack token alone cannot distinguish token-validation behavior from broken client/app configuration.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against Logto-issued JWTs, the verifier configuration MUST check `iss` against the tenant issuer `https://<tenant>/oidc` (or discovery `issuer`). Testing without issuer validation is invalid because Logto documentation expects issuer comparison as part of token validation.

For I5 audience-validation tests against Logto-issued JWTs, the verifier MUST manually validate `aud` against the API resource indicator or organization audience/context as appropriate. Several code examples disable library-level audience verification and instruct developers to verify audience manually based on the permission model; a test that omits this check is invalid.

For I5 organization-context tests, the verifier MUST validate both permissions and context: check `organization_id` and the relevant audience form (API resource and/or organization audience) rather than scopes alone. Logto explicitly requires validating both permissions and context for secure multi-tenant APIs.

For token-exchange tests, the target application MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled first. Logto disables token exchange by default; otherwise the endpoint returns 'token exchange is not allowed for this application', which is setup failure rather than a security result.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scopes/claims against upstream authorization intent. Logto states PAT-obtained and refresh-token-obtained access tokens follow the same authorization patterns, so exchanged tokens should not be interpreted as a separate privilege model.

For sign-out / revocation freshness tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish token revocation from end-session behavior. End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` may remain valid until grant TTL expiry unless explicitly revoked. Use `/oidc/token/revocation` when the test requires token invalidation.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. The documentation does not define `0` as disable or immediate expiry. Never assume `0` is a special sentinel for token lifetime; use explicit positive values and treat omitted value as default 3600s.

Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token `expiresIn` has a documented default of 600 seconds (10 minutes) when unspecified. Do not assume omission means no expiry; omission selects the default limited lifetime.

For I2 key-rotation coherence tests, Cloud tenants apply new signing keys immediately after rotation, but JWKS consumers may cache keys. The fuzzer MUST only flag old-key acceptance after the verifier's JWKS cache has been refreshed or cache TTL has expired; otherwise acceptance may be due to normal JWKS caching.
oidc_jwt.source: developers/signing-keys.mdx; authorization/validate-access-tokens/* examples using JWKS caching

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in `/oidc/token` and the resulting `aud` claim must exactly match the registered API resource indicator URI. Logto documentation explicitly states exact matching; do not use prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like substitutes.

For I5 empty-audience and opaque-vs-JWT tests, if no `resource` is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. To test JWT audience enforcement, always request a concrete `resource` or configure a default API resource; otherwise failures may reflect token format differences rather than audience validation.

For I5 default-resource tests, when a default API resource is configured and the `resource` parameter is omitted, Logto uses that default API resource as the audience for access tokens. Do not interpret acceptance without an explicit `resource` as missing audience validation unless no default API resource is configured.

For I5 scope tests, requested scope names must exactly match permission names defined on the API resource. Logto does not support wildcard, prefix, or shortened scope matching. For multi-permission scenarios, request each exact scope string explicitly.

For I5 organization-bound authorization tests, organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. Configure tests separately for global-resource and organization-resource scenarios or results will be misinterpreted.

For I5 organization token tests, include `organization_id` in `/oidc/token` requests when testing organization permissions or organization-level API resources. Without `organization_id`, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced.

For I5 organization-level API tests, request both `resource` and `organization_id` in `/oidc/token`. Omitting `resource` changes token type/target, while omitting `organization_id` disables organization RBAC and only global permissions are considered.

For I5 permission-change sequences, Logto JWTs are immutable after issuance. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid test must obtain a fresh token after changing roles/permissions; reusing an old token is expected to preserve old scopes until expiry.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes that were not part of the original OAuth authorization request will NOT appear through refresh. The client must run a new authorization flow. Do not treat absence of newly granted scopes after refresh as a bug.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on organization tokens, enlarged permissions appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but still require a new token. If the new scopes exceed the original request set, a full new authorization flow is required.

For I2 expired-token tests, use a control token with a valid `exp` and compare against an expired token. Logto documentation requires expiration validation for access tokens; without a control, a 401 may reflect bad client configuration or wrong audience/scope rather than expiry enforcement.

For I2 future-token and `nbf` tests, Logto documentation in the provided material does not state that `nbf` is enforced for access tokens. Acceptance of a future-`nbf` token should not be treated as a vulnerability without separate evidence; use `exp`-based freshness tests as the primary oracle.

For I3 sign-out and revocation tests, Logto sign-out is multi-layered: clearing client-side tokens only signs out the local app, while redirecting to `/oidc/session/end` clears the centralized Logto session. Do not treat continued SSO after local token deletion as a session revocation failure.

For I3 logout/grant-coherence tests, if the app has `offline_access`, end-session does not revoke that app grant by default. Refresh-token-based access may continue until grant expiry unless the token/grant is explicitly revoked. Do not flag this as stale authorization without explicit revocation.

For I3 token-exchange tests, the application must have token exchange explicitly enabled in application settings. If not enabled, `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` will fail by design with a 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' error.

For I3 OIDC flow tests, Logto uses standard authorization code flow with PKCE and redirects. `start_oidc_auth` must preserve and later verify `state`, and `exchange_code_for_token` must use the matching `code_verifier`. Failures from mismatched state or PKCE are expected flow protections, not identity bugs.

For I3 organization-token acquisition tests, organization tokens cannot currently be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. You must first obtain a refresh token, then call `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` plus organization parameters. Testing direct code-to-organization-token issuance will produce false failures.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against Logto-issued JWTs, validate `iss` against the tenant issuer from `/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `https://<tenant>/oidc`. The docs state issuer is fixed and not customizable; do not assume alternate issuer aliases.

For I1 signature-validation and key-rotation tests, verify JWTs against the tenant JWKS at `/oidc/jwks`. After signing key rotation, Cloud tenants apply the new key immediately, but existing tokens signed by the previous key remain valid until expiry while the previous key remains published. Do not treat acceptance of already-issued old tokens as a trust-anchor failure.

For I1 consecutive key-rotation tests, Logto documentation warns never to rotate signing keys consecutively because this may invalidate all issued tokens. Avoid multi-rotation sequences as a coherence oracle; they can create platform-induced invalidation unrelated to the tested invariant.

For I4 enterprise SSO identity-binding tests, Logto automatically links an enterprise SSO identity to an existing user account when the working email matches an existing user. Different upstream identities collapsing into one downstream account by matching email is documented behavior; collision tests must account for this linking rule.

For I4 enterprise connector tests, once an email domain is associated with an enterprise SSO connector, existing users with that domain are restricted to sign in with that enterprise SSO connector and previous sign-in methods are blocked. Do not interpret blocked password/social login as an authorization regression.

For I4 connector-identity tests, connector `target` values are identity-provider names and must be unique per platform. Documentation warns that different IdPs configured with the same `target` can cause users to sign in to accounts created with another provider's identity. Multi-provider collision tests must model `target` uniqueness carefully.

For I4 same-IdP tests, using the same IdP with different connector `target` values intentionally creates separate Logto accounts even for the same upstream identity. Do not flag this as an identity split bug; it is documented connector behavior.

For I5 PAT token-exchange tests, access tokens obtained via personal access token exchange are documented to behave identically to tokens obtained through the standard refresh-token flow. Do not treat PAT-based access as a separate authorization model; apply the same audience, scope, and organization expectations.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in `/oidc/auth` and `/oidc/token` MUST exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator URI. Logto documentation states exact matching only; prefixes or shortened values are not wildcards. Do NOT use `*` or partial strings.

For I5 organization-context tests, `organization_id` MUST be included when requesting organization tokens or organization-level API tokens. If omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated and organization RBAC is not enforced.

For I5 mixed-scope tests, organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. A test that combines them may fail by design rather than exposing escalation.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not modified after role/permission changes. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens. A valid coherence test must obtain a NEW token after the config change; reusing an old token is expected to preserve old scopes until expiry.

For I5 organization-token enlargement tests, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance via refresh or token request, but only within the originally requested scope set. If the new scopes exceed the original request, a new authorization flow is still required.

For I2 freshness tests against JWT expiration, include a control token request that should succeed alongside the expired/future-token attempt. Use valid claims such as exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} for the control. Without a control, rejection may reflect broken client/app configuration rather than time validation.

Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token `expiresIn` has a documented default of 10 minutes if not specified. Do not assume omission means no expiry. Tests involving magic-link freshness must account for the default nonzero lifetime.

For I2 sign-out/revocation tests, end-session and token revocation are not equivalent in Logto. If `offline_access` was granted, ending the centralized Logto session does NOT revoke the app grant by default; refresh-token-based access may continue until grant expiry unless the token/grant is explicitly revoked.

For I2 logout persistence tests, Logto grant TTL defaults to 180 days. If `offline_access` is present, refresh-token chains may remain valid until grant expiry. Do not interpret post-logout refresh success as a vulnerability unless explicit revocation was expected and tested.

For I3 sign-out coherence tests, current SDK `signOut()` behavior performs global sign-out by redirecting through `/session/end` and `/session/end/confirm` with `logout=true`. Tests must distinguish client-local logout from centralized Logto session termination.

For I3 key-rotation tests, never rotate signing keys consecutively two or more times. Documentation warns this may invalidate all issued tokens. A valid rotation test should perform a single rotation and then test old-vs-new key acceptance.

For I3 key-rotation tests on OSS deployments, a Logto instance restart is required after rotating the signing key before the new key takes effect. Without restart, stale acceptance/rejection results are not meaningful.

For I1 trust-anchor rotation tests on Cloud, new signing keys take effect immediately after rotation, but old tokens signed by previous keys remain valid until those previous keys are removed. Do not flag acceptance of tokens signed by a documented 'previous' key as a bug before key removal.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the expected issuer is fixed to `https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc` and Logto does not allow customizing issuer or JWKS URI independently. Tests must compare against the tenant OIDC issuer from discovery or this fixed pattern, not an arbitrary configured issuer.

For I1 audience-validation tests in backend examples, several validation snippets set library-level `verify_aud` or `ValidateAudience` to false and require manual audience checking based on permission model. A test harness MUST explicitly validate `aud` against the requested API resource or organization audience; otherwise acceptance is by incomplete verifier configuration, not necessarily a platform flaw.

For I5 scope-binding tests, scope names must exactly match permission names defined in the API resource. There is no wildcard, prefix, or shorthand matching. If multiple different permissions are needed, request each exact scope explicitly.

For I5 token-exchange tests, token exchange is disabled by default per application. The target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled before any RFC 8693 test; otherwise rejection is expected and not evidence of proper audience/scope enforcement.

For I5 PAT token-exchange tests, `subject_token_type` must be `urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token`. Using a PAT with a generic access-token subject type is incorrect setup and invalidates the test.

For I5 impersonation token-exchange tests, if an `actor_token` is supplied, it should be a valid access token for the acting user and the resulting token may include an `act.sub` claim. Do not treat presence of `act` as identity confusion; it is explicit impersonation context.

For I2 replay tests on impersonation subject tokens, the documentation states the subject token is short-lived and one-time-use. Replay expectations differ from normal bearer JWTs; only the subject token itself should be treated as one-time, not the exchanged access token.

For I3 OIDC flow tests, Logto enforces PKCE and disables insecure implicit flow. Authorization-code tests should include PKCE parameters (`code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, later `code_verifier`) to avoid false failures caused by missing required flow binding.

For I1/I5 cross-provider direct-sign-in tests, `direct_sign_in` values are structured identifiers, not patterns: social uses `social:<idp-name>` and enterprise SSO uses `sso:<connector-id>`. These are exact identifiers; do not use wildcard-like values.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
